QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_1

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, a new IC member at Lotus Capital AIF (a Category II private equity fund), is preparing an induction note on the Indian AIF industry's regulatory timeline. Which of the following correctly identifies the regulatory watershed that transformed the erstwhile VC/PE industry in India into a full-fledged 'AIF industry' and provided the current legal framework for Cat I and II managers?

answer.text: The notification of the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, under which Category I, II and III AIFs are registered
The SEBI (Venture Capital Fund) Regulations, 1996, which first brought unlisted-company investing under SEBI purview
The K.B. Chandrasekhar Committee recommendations of 2000, which introduced fund-level tax pass-through for VCFs
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, which created the operating space for Special Situations Funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 3, the AIF industry in its present form was created by the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012. The 2011-2019 period is described as the 'consolidation and transformation' phase during which the VC/PE industry transformed into an AIF industry. All three AIF categories are registered under the 2012 AIF Regulations. The Trap: The 1996 VCF Regulations only covered VC funds, not the broader AIF universe, and were superseded. The 2000 Chandrasekhar Committee recommendations refined VCF rules but did not create the AIF framework. The IBC 2016 enabled SSF opportunities but does not itself regulate AIFs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) and XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) both test the 2012 Regulations as the governing law. XIX-E (future Cat III Managers) will also sit under the same 2012 Regulations. The IBC linkage is tested more deeply in XV (Research Analyst) stressed-asset modules. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II managers should cite the 2012 Regulations (and the specific amendment year, e.g., 2022 for SSF, 2023 for CDMDF, 2024 for VCF definition) in every PPM 'Regulatory Framework' section. LPs' legal counsel will reject PPMs that rely on superseded 1996 VCF Regulations language.
